summaryText:
Pastor Ryan taught a message titled Plan It in Prayer, encouraging the congregation to write it down and treat prayer as a planned, daily practice rather than something we only do in reaction to circumstances. He opened by calling the church to come with reverence and expectation, and he challenged listeners to ask whether they are truly God's people, marked by the discipleship Jesus described: denying ourselves, taking up our cross, and following him. Drawing on 2 Chronicles 7:14, he explained that God invites his people to humble themselves, pray, seek his face, and turn from sin. He noted that many believers grow discouraged in prayer or have simply never been taught how to pray.

Using Matthew 6 as the main text, Pastor Ryan pointed out that the disciples never asked Jesus to teach them miracles or public ministry. They asked him to teach them to pray, likely because they saw how his ministry flowed from time alone with the Father. Jesus first teaches how not to pray: not to be seen by others (verses 5 and 6) and not with empty, repeated phrases meant to impress (verses 7 and 8). Pastor Ryan encouraged listeners to choose a simple time and place for prayer, even an ordinary one like a car, and to pray honestly. God is not impressed by polished words, he said, but by an honest heart. He also reminded the church that prayer is a conversation, so we should make room to listen. He warned against wanting influence without intimacy with God.

He then walked through the Lord's Prayer as a template (verses 9 to 13). We come to God as our Father with confidence, and as the Holy One with reverence. We pray for his kingdom first, including the gospel, disciples, missionaries, and churches. We ask for our daily needs and trust God for fresh provision each day. We confess our sin and forgive others, remembering how much we have been forgiven. We ask the Holy Spirit for guidance and protection from temptation. Pastor Ryan acknowledged the real hurts many people carry and encouraged releasing unforgiveness as a step toward freedom.

The service closed with invitations. Those who want to grow in prayer were invited to lift their hands as a sign of surrender. Those who do not yet know Jesus were invited to receive him as Lord and Savior, and the church prayed together. The prayer team was available at the altar. Pastor Ryan's heart was to put practical tools in people's hands so that when Monday morning comes, they know how to pray.
mainPoints: Jesus teaches us to pray honestly and in secret, not to be seen or to impress God, so we need a regular time and place to meet with the Father.

The Lord's Prayer is a template for praying: come to our holy Father with confidence and reverence, seek his kingdom first, ask for daily needs, confess sin and forgive others, and ask the Holy Spirit for guidance.
God's people are called to be a praying people who humble themselves, repent, and seek intimacy with God before influence, trusting that prayer moves the hand of God.

Monday.scripture: Luke 11:1 - "Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples."
Monday.focus: Come to Jesus with the humble heart of a learner, asking him to teach you how to pray.
Monday.action: Write "Plan it in prayer" at the top of a notebook. Choose one realistic time and place this week for prayer (a car, a closet, a quiet corner) and write it down.
Monday.prayer: Lord, teach me to pray. Remove any ideas about prayer that do not line up with your Word, and help me pray the way you want me to. In Jesus' name, amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Matthew 6:6 - "But when you pray, go into your room, close the door and pray to your Father, who is unseen."
Tuesday.focus: Meet with the Father in the secret place, where no one is watching but God.
Tuesday.action: Go to your chosen place at your chosen time. Silence your phone and pray for five minutes, even if you get distracted. Gently return to prayer each time.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, I come to you in secret, not to be seen by anyone else. I want your approval more than the approval of people. Meet me here today. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Matthew 6:8 - "Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him."
Wednesday.focus: Pray honestly instead of trying to impress God, and make room to listen.
Wednesday.action: Pray one plain, honest prayer about what is really on your heart, in your own words. Then sit quietly for one minute and listen, writing down anything that comes to mind.
Wednesday.prayer: God, I do not have to impress you. I need your help and I am being honest with you. Quiet my heart so I can hear you. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Matthew 6:33 - "But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well."
Thursday.focus: Pray for God's kingdom first: his name honored, the gospel preached, and disciples made.
Thursday.action: Before praying about your own needs, spend a few minutes praying for kingdom things: the gospel going forward, our church, missionaries, and one person who does not yet know Jesus.
Thursday.prayer: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come and your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give me a burden for the things that matter to your heart. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Matthew 6:12 - "And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors."
Friday.focus: Bring your daily needs to God, confess sin, and release unforgiveness.
Friday.action: Write down your needs for today and bring them to God. Then confess anything the Holy Spirit brings to mind. If there is someone you need to forgive, name them before God and ask for strength to let them go.
Friday.prayer: Father, thank you for providing what I need today. Forgive me for my sin, and help me forgive those who have hurt me, remembering how much you have forgiven me. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Matthew 6:13 - "And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one."
Saturday.focus: Ask the Holy Spirit for guidance and protection, and look ahead to worshiping with your church family.
Saturday.action: Before asking others or checking your phone, ask the Holy Spirit for direction on one decision or struggle. Then plan your prayer time for next week and consider inviting a friend or family member to pray with you.
Saturday.prayer: Holy Spirit, lead me and guide me. Keep me from temptation and deliver me from evil. For yours is the kingdom, and all glory and honor belong to you. Amen.
